title: Combined Work: Add Rates, Not Days
excerpt: If A and B together finish in 15 days and B alone in 20 days, A alone takes 60 days — you add work *rates*, not days.
author: BountyCode Team
body:
## The rule

If A completes work in n days, A's 1 day's work = 1/n.
Combined rate = sum of individual rates.

If A+B finish in 15 days and B alone in 20:
A alone = (15 × 20) ÷ (20 − 15) = 300 ÷ 5 = 60 days.

## The trap

Never subtract days (20 − 15 = 5). Subtract rates (1/15 − 1/20).

## Practice it

Drill combined-work and work-wages questions in the Time & Work topic test.
code:
from fractions import Fraction
ab = Fraction(1, 15)
b = Fraction(1, 20)
a = ab - b          # 1/60
print('A alone:', 1 / a)   # 60 days
